public_health_question.v: What were the sources and modes of transmission of two Norwalk-like virus gastroenteritis outbreaks, one foodborne in Alaska and one person-to-person in Wisconsin?

ev.q: This report presents investigations of a foodborne NLV outbreak in Alaska and person-to-person transmission in Wisconsin.
Outbreaks of Norwalk-like Viral Gastroenteritis --- Alaska and Wisconsin, 1999
This report presents investigations of a foodborne NLV outbreak in Alaska and person-to-person transmission in Wisconsin.
On November 11, questionnaires were e-mailed to 500 company employees; 456 (91%) were returned.
All residents of the involved floor were administered a symptom, event, and food history questionnaire.
Outbreaks of Norwalk-like Viral Gastroenteritis --- Alaska and Wisconsin, 1999

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension is analyzed; populations are company employees and university residence-hall students, and shared living is framed as a transmission setting, not social position.

notes: Median incubation (33 hours) and illness durations are reported descriptively and not compared, so outcome_types stays binary/categorical. RT-PCR and sequencing confirm case status and link the foodhandler; they are not procedures. Wisconsin illness clustering into generations (Figure 2) is descriptive.
view_issues: Figures 1 and 2 are shown only as images, with no description in the text.
